steps.note: One step. The request is checked against the monthly paid leave allowance on the employee's record, and the remaining paid leave is shown before they submit (BR-2) — an employee should know whether the days are paid before they take them.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Dates out of order, a range with no working day, an overlap with approved leave and a missing reason all arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request, its counted days and the paid-versus-unpaid split together or not at all. Nothing is authorised — the days are not written into attendance until the approver approves it (BR-7). Off-days and holidays in the range are excluded and not consumed, because an employee should not spend leave on a day the school was shut (BR-8).

operations.name: staff.leave.request
operations.idempotencyKey: staff_id + from_date + to_date, since an employee carries one request per date range
operations.purpose: Submit a staff leave request, checked against the monthly paid allowance.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The requesting employee's own record. Any employee may request leave; it is not a privilege of one classification (BR-1).

parameters.name: leave_type
parameters.type: enum: Casual | Sick | Annual | Unpaid | Bereavement | Maternity or paternity
parameters.notes: What the leave is for. The employee's own word — a type chosen for them describes their circumstances.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The first day of the leave.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.notes: On or after the from date (E1).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters, written by the employee (E4). What the approver weighs.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The request, with what is paid and what is not.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: The request.

fields.name: days_counted
fields.description: The working days it covers, with off-days and holidays excluded (BR-8).

fields.name: dates_excluded
fields.description: Closed days inside the range, not consumed by the leave (BR-8).

fields.name: allowance_remaining
fields.description: How much paid leave is left this month, from the figure on the staff record (BR-2).

fields.name: paid_days
fields.description: Days covered by the remaining allowance (BR-6).

fields.name: unpaid_days
fields.description: Days beyond it, which payroll deducts at the daily rate (BR-6, UC-12-03 BR-4).

fields.name: approver
fields.description: The right approver for this employee under the configured chain (BR-4). Never the requester (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The to date is before the from date.
The range contains no working day.
errors.note: An employee should not spend leave on a day the school was shut (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The dates overlap leave already approved for this employee.
errors.note: The message names the covered dates (BR-11).

errors.meaning: The employee's staff record carries no leave allowance.
errors.note: The request cannot be assessed — paid and unpaid days cannot be told apart (BR-2, UC-12-01 BR-4).

errors.meaning: The employee is their own approver under the configured chain.
errors.note: The configuration is flagged. Nobody approves their own leave (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the leave type. Casual, sick, annual and unpaid describe different circumstances (BR-6), and one picked for an employee is the school characterising why they were away.
Never compose the reason. It is what the approver weighs (E4), and a refusal is answered against it.
Report the paid and unpaid split before anything else. An employee should know whether the days are paid before they take them (BR-2), and unpaid days are deducted at the daily rate.
Report the days excluded as closed. Off-days and holidays are not consumed by the leave (BR-8), so a Thursday-to-Monday request may count two days rather than five.
Never approve in the same plan. Nobody approves their own leave, and the chain exists for that reason (BR-3, E7).
Report a self-approver configuration as a configuration fault, not a refusal of the leave. The chain has put the employee at both ends and somebody has to fix it (E5).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A request is approved, rejected, or cancelled by the employee before it starts, which restores the allowance (BR-10).

intent.name: staff.leave.approve
intent.summary: Approve a staff leave request, which codes the days in attendance and makes the employee unavailable. The configured approver only, one step.

request.text: chhutti rad kar do
hazri mein chhutti laga do

routesElsewhere.note: Approved leave is written into the attendance record and codes those days as leave rather than absent (BR-7).

request.text: in dinon ka cover laga do

routesElsewhere.note: Approved leave makes the employee unavailable, which blocks a timetable assignment in that slot and is read when arranging cover (BR-12). Arranging it is a separate act.

steps.note: One step, and it reaches attendance, payroll and the timetable. Approved leave is written into the attendance record and codes those days as leave rather than absent — the two are treated differently by payroll and by any disciplinary process (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An approver acting on their own request is refused by the API.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the attendance days coded as leave, the reduced allowance and the message to the employee together or not at all. Days within the allowance are paid; days beyond it are unpaid and deducted by payroll at the daily rate (BR-6). The employee becomes unavailable for those days, which blocks a timetable assignment in that slot and is read when arranging cover (BR-12).

operations.name: staff.leave.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a request carries one approval and a repeat must not write the days twice
operations.purpose: Approve the leave request and write the days into attendance.

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with the employee, the dates, the type and the status.

errors.meaning: The actor is the employee whose request it is.
The actor is not the approver for this employee under the configured chain.
errors.note: Staff leave goes to the School Admin, theirs to the Principal, and the Principal's to the Super Admin (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A leave day arrives after attendance was already marked.
errors.written: The leave is approved and the attendance amended.
errors.notWritten: Nothing lost — the original mark is kept.

planningRules.rule: Never approve a request the actor made. E7 is BR-3 working, and the configured chain exists precisely so that nobody signs off their own absence.
Report the paid and unpaid days at approval. The unpaid ones are deducted by payroll at the daily rate (BR-6), and the approver is agreeing to leave that costs the employee money.
Report where attendance was already marked and has been amended. The original mark is kept (E9), and whoever marked the employee absent should know it now reads as leave.
Report the timetable slots the employee can no longer be assigned to. Approved leave makes them unavailable and blocks an assignment in that slot (BR-12) — somebody has to arrange cover.
Never chain cover onto the approval. Who covers a period is a decision about a class, taken against a clash check of its own.

reversal.statement: An approval is not withdrawn. The employee may cancel before the start date, which restores the allowance; after it has begun, days already passed stand and only the remaining days can be cancelled (BR-10, E10).

intent.name: staff.leave.reject
intent.summary: Reject a staff leave request with the written reason. The configured approver only, one step.

routesElsewhere.note: A request is approved or rejected as it stands. Shorter leave is a fresh request from the employee.

steps.note: One step. A rejection carries a written reason — an employee refused leave with no explanation cannot plan around it or appeal it (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A rejection with no reason is not recorded at all.
plan.atomicity: One write: the rejection, its reason and the message to the employee together or not at all. The allowance is untouched, nothing is written into attendance, and the employee remains available for the timetable. They are told either way — a request that disappears is worse than one that is refused (BR-9).

routesElsewhere.note: Changing the dates is cancelling one request and submitting another, which is checked against the allowance again.

steps.note: One step. A request may be cancelled before its start date and the allowance is restored — an employee who came in after all should not have spent leave (BR-10).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report, with one exception: a cancellation after the leave has begun is handled rather than refused — days already passed stand and the remaining days are cancelled (E10).
plan.atomicity: One write: the cancellation, the restored allowance and the reverted attendance days together or not at all. Days already passed stand as leave; only the remaining days come back (BR-10, E10). The employee becomes available again for the timetable on the days that reverted (BR-12).

operations.name: staff.leave.cancel
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a request is cancelled once
operations.purpose: Cancel a leave request, restoring the allowance for days not yet taken.

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No leave request matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with the employee, the dates, the type and the status.

parameters.notes: The leave request, resolved from the employee and the dates.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.description: The request.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Cancelled. Terminal.

fields.name: days_reverted
fields.description: Leave days removed from attendance. The employee is markable normally again (BR-10).

fields.name: days_retained
fields.description: Days already passed, which stand as leave (E10).

fields.name: allowance_restored
fields.description: Paid days returned to the month's allowance (BR-10).

fields.name: allowance_remaining
fields.description: What the employee now has left this month.

fields.description: Timetable slots the employee can be assigned to again (BR-12).

errors.meaning: The employee cancelled after the leave had begun.
errors.note: Not a refusal. Report both lists (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The request is rejected or already cancelled.

planningRules.rule: Never cancel on the school's behalf. Cancelling is the employee's act; refusing leave is the approver's, and they are different records with different meanings (BR-5, BR-10).

Report which days reverted and which stand. Once the leave has begun only the remaining days are cancelled (E10), and an employee expecting the whole request withdrawn will be surprised by a spent allowance.
Report the allowance restored. It is the point of cancelling — an employee who came in after all should not have spent leave (BR-10).
Never chain a fresh request onto a cancellation. Changing the dates is two acts, and the new dates are the employee's to state and are checked against the allowance again.

reversal.statement: Cancelled is terminal. Leave needed after all is a fresh request, assessed against the allowance as it now stands.
